\section[ai]{\ta{ஐ} — the letter that opens \ta{ஐந்து}}

\label{lesson:TA-S134-letter-ai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: read \ta{◌ீ} and \ta{◌ெ} aloud, and write each once.

Now say \textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}} (\emph{aintu}), \textquotedblleft{}five\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ta{ஐ}}
\textbf{\ta{ஐ}} — \emph{ai}.

It opens \textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}} (\emph{aintu}), \textquotedblleft{}five\textquotedblright{}. You wrote its sign \ta{◌ை} two chapters ago, on the end of \ta{இல்லை}. This is the \textbf{independent} shape of the same vowel, for a word that begins with \emph{ai}.

\subsection*{Writing: \ta{ஐ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/TA-S134-letter-ai-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ta{ஐ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: curl inward around the upper-left spiral, then lift
  \item \textbf{2.} put the pen down again and draw the central upright upward, then lift
  \item \textbf{3.} put the pen down again and sweep around the upper-right loop and return left across the middle, then lift
  \item \textbf{4.} put the pen down again and circle the lower-left bowl back toward the centre, then lift
  \item \textbf{5.} put the pen down again and descend and circle through the lower-right bowl — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 4.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Info-farmer, Writing Tamil 10.gif, \ta{ஐ} stroke-order animation (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0, 2008), cross-checked with Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I Frame 11 (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}} and point at \ta{ஐ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ta{ஐ} three times, saying \emph{ai} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ta{◌ெ}, then \ta{ஐ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which character is this — \ta{ஐ}? (\textbf{ai}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}}, \emph{aintu}, \textquotedblleft{}five\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ū]{\ta{◌ூ} — the long u on \ta{மூன்று}}

\label{lesson:TA-S135-vowel-sign-uu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: read \ta{◌ெ} and \ta{ஐ} aloud, and write each once.

Now say \textbf{\ta{மூன்று}} (\emph{mūṉṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}three\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ta{◌ூ}}
\textbf{\ta{◌ூ}} — \emph{ū}.

It is the long \emph{ū} on \textbf{\ta{மூன்று}} (\emph{mūṉṟu}), \textquotedblleft{}three\textquotedblright{}. Like its short partner \ta{◌ு}, which you already write, this sign changes shape with the consonant it joins, so copy it as it sits on \textbf{\ta{மூ}}, the form you already read.

\subsection*{Writing: \ta{◌ூ}}
Put your pen on \ta{◌ூ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start the character or which way to travel}. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ta{மூன்று}} and point at \ta{◌ூ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ta{◌ூ} three times, saying \emph{ū} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ta{ஐ}, then \ta{◌ூ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ta{மூன்று}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which character is this — \ta{◌ூ}? (\textbf{ū}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ta{மூன்று}}, \emph{mūṉṟu}, \textquotedblleft{}three\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ē]{\ta{ஏ} — the letter that opens \ta{ஏழு}}

\label{lesson:TA-S136-letter-ee}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: read \ta{ஐ} and \ta{◌ூ} aloud, and write each once.

Now say \textbf{\ta{ஏழு}} (\emph{ēḻu}), \textquotedblleft{}seven\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ta{ஏ}}
\textbf{\ta{ஏ}} — \emph{ē}.

It opens \textbf{\ta{ஏழு}} (\emph{ēḻu}), \textquotedblleft{}seven\textquotedblright{}. You already write its sign \ta{◌ே} from \ta{பேசு}; \ta{ஏ} is the independent shape of the same long vowel, for the front of a word.

\subsection*{Writing: \ta{ஏ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/TA-S136-letter-ee-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ta{ஏ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep from the inner curl around the broad left loop
  \item \textbf{2.} without lifting, climb the outer left side into the crown
  \item \textbf{3.} without lifting, carry the top bar to the right
  \item \textbf{4.} without lifting, retrace left and draw the right upright down
  \item \textbf{5.} without lifting, continue down-left along the diagonal foot
  \item \textbf{6.} without lifting, turn at the foot and finish back up-right — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 0.} The pen never leaves the paper.

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Module 7, \ta{ஏ}, with Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 7 (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ta{ஏழு}} and point at \ta{ஏ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ta{ஏ} three times, saying \emph{ē} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ta{◌ூ}, then \ta{ஏ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ta{ஏழு}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which character is this — \ta{ஏ}? (\textbf{ē}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ta{ஏழு}}, \emph{ēḻu}, \textquotedblleft{}seven\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
